category: exploratory synthetic engineering and identifiability probe
hypothesis: Mapping-level FK identity with declaration multiplicity metadata can be represented by one reified node per unique Join mapping, allowing the frozen official G-reasoner to emit a separate stable node score for same-endpoint FK candidates; a small synthetic query set may reveal an initial signal.

predecessors.duplicate_identity_policy: EXPLORATORY_COMPLETE; mapping identity 99 unique mappings, 198 directed edges, multiplicity metadata retained

methods: local Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B dense cosine over mapping descriptions
direct typed multi-edge table graph; node-level output only
reified relation-typed graph with one node per unique mapping
simple FK path baseline, expected tie on the shared one-hop endpoint path

success_criteria.mapping_identity: 3 declarations derive 2 stable IDs by SHA-256 of ordered (source_table, source_column, target_table, target_column) tuples with billing multiplicity 2 and shipping multiplicity 1; reversing declarations preserves IDs and counts
success_criteria.model_output: direct graph output [1,2], reified output [1,4], all finite
success_criteria.permutation: mapping-node scores remain attached to stable IDs after node and edge reordering; mapping-only max absolute delta <= 1e-5 and top-ranked mapping ID set unchanged
success_criteria.synthetic_signal: GFM top-1 correct on at least 3/4 fixed queries, correct on strictly more queries than dense cosine, and mean score margin is positive for both billing and shipping query groups
success_criteria.baseline_evidence: report exact candidate scores/ranks for dense cosine, reified GFM, and path baseline; report direct graph table-node scores/ranks and state mapping rank is unavailable
success_criteria.overall_status: G0_SYNTHETIC_PASS only if interface, permutation, and synthetic signal criteria all pass; otherwise G0_SYNTHETIC_NO_GO or implementation failure

budget.rss_limit_rationale: A 0.6B-parameter encoder requires about 2.24 GiB for FP32 weights alone; 8 GiB allows model/runtime overhead while remaining a bounded cap on the 503 GiB host. This is a conservative estimate, not a measured peak.
